# Small working example

```{r}
library(GeoNonStat)
```


Generating fake observations: locations, observed variable (field) and covariates (to explain field, range and noise), for example purpose.

```{r}
set.seed(100)
nobs <- 10000
observed_locs <- cbind(runif(5000), runif(5000))
observed_locs <- observed_locs[sample(seq_len(5000), nobs, replace = TRUE), ]
observed_field <- rnorm(nobs)
Xfield <- as.data.frame(cbind(runif(nobs), rnorm(nobs), rpois(nobs, 3)))
Xrange <- as.data.frame(cbind(runif(nobs), rnorm(nobs)))
Xnoise <- as.data.frame(cbind(runif(nobs), rnorm(nobs)))
```

You can create a vecchia approximation associated with your locations,
choosing the number of nearest neighbors:

```{r}
my_vecchia_approx <- createVecchia(observed_locs, m=6)
```

From the vecchia approximation, you can model prediction points (PP) 
for the noise and range of you locations, based on the vecchia approximation, 
if needed.
TODO : expliquer pourquoi on ne le ferait pas ? 

Here we will model only PP for noise. 

```{r}
noise_PP <- createPP(
  vecchia_approx = vecchia_approx,
  matern_range = .1,
  knots = 50,
  plot = FALSE
)
```

We can now create a GeoNonStat object that will be used to model and 
predict the observed field :

```{r}
my_data <- list(
  observed_field = observed_field,
  X = Xfield,
  range_X = Xrange,
  noise_X  = Xnoise
)

myobj <- GeoNonStat(
  vecchia_approx = vecchia_approx,
  data_list = my_data,
  matern_smoothness = 1.5, # Matern smoothness
  anisotropic = FALSE,
  n_chains = 3,
  noise_PP = noise_PP,
  noise_log_scale_bounds = c(-8, 3),
  range_PP = NULL
)

summary(myobj)
myobj
estimate(processedGnsDemo)
# Recreating new data with less observations but same structure as example data
locs <- cbind(rnorm(200), rnorm(200))
X <- data.frame(matrix(rnorm(200*4), ncol=4))
colnames(X) <- paste0("V", 1:4)
testdata <- list("locs" = locs, "X" = X, noise_X=X)  
testpredictions <- predict(processedGnsDemo, list(testdata))
```
